analysis.summary: Belgium open Group G as clear favorites against an Egypt side whose best player, Mohamed Salah, is managing a hamstring injury and may be limited to a substitute role. The Red Devils boast superior squad depth and quality on paper — De Bruyne is fit and expected to start — but a makeshift defense (Zeno Debast absent through injury) and an out-of-form Lukaku reduce their ceiling. Egypt's AFCON semi-final pedigree and a head-to-head record that strongly favors them (3 wins from 4 meetings) means an upset is genuinely possible, though Belgium's dominant pre-tournament form (5-2 vs USA, 5-0 vs Tunisia) signals real momentum.
analysis.home_form: Belgium went unbeaten through World Cup qualification, scoring 29 goals and conceding 7 across 10 games. Under Rudi Garcia, they won 5-2 vs USA, drew 1-1 vs Mexico, beat Croatia 2-0, and routed Tunisia 5-0 in warmups. Their 4-2-3-1 system centers on De Bruyne as the no.10, flanked by Doku (returned to training after a minor concern) and Trossard, with De Ketelaere as a false nine or second striker.
analysis.away_form: Egypt topped their CAF qualifying group unbeaten, winning 8 of 10 games; Mohamed Salah contributed 9 qualifying goals. At AFCON 2025 they reached the semi-finals before losing to Senegal, keeping two clean sheets in three group games. Salah suffered a hamstring injury late in the Liverpool season but played 45 minutes off the bench vs Brazil on June 6. Omar Marmoush (Manchester City) provides a dangerous alternative attacking threat.
analysis.h2h: Belgium and Egypt have met four times, all in friendlies: Egypt won 1-0 (Mar 1999), Egypt won 4-0 (Feb 2005), Belgium won 3-0 (Jun 2018), Egypt won 2-1 (Nov 2022). Egypt lead the all-time series 3-1. Belgium's sole win came in a 2018 World Cup warmup. The most recent meeting in 2022 ended 2-1 to Egypt, suggesting the Africans can compete when motivated.
injuries_news: Belgium: Zeno Debast (central defender) is out with a leg injury suffered in May — a notable absence in the backline. Romeo Lavia was excluded from the squad after another injury-hit season. Romelu Lukaku is included despite chronic muscle injuries at Napoli (only ~60 minutes of competitive football in 2025-26); coach Garcia admitted he is 'out of shape' and unlikely to start.
Belgium: Jeremy Doku had a minor fitness concern but returned to training and is expected to start.
Egypt: Mohamed Salah is managing a hamstring injury from the Liverpool season; he played 45 minutes vs Brazil on June 6 and is expected to start or feature significantly, but is not at 100% fitness.
Egypt: No other confirmed injury concerns in the squad; Hossam Hassan expected to field a near full-strength XI.
key_factors: Belgium's defensive vulnerability: the absence of Debast and Lukaku's limited fitness shift the balance of power slightly. Garcia's back four looks makeshift and can be exploited by Egypt's pace on the counter.
Salah's fitness is the key swing factor for Egypt: a fully fit Salah would shift Egypt's probability meaningfully upward; even a limited Salah provides quality and set-piece threat.
Omar Marmoush (Manchester City) is in peak form and gives Egypt a genuine Premier League-level forward even if Salah is managed.

Belgium's attacking firepower (De Bruyne, Doku, Trossard, De Ketelaere) should ultimately prove too much for Egypt over 90 minutes, and the Red Devils' warmup results indicate they are in excellent form.
Lumen Field is at near sea-level (Seattle, ~10 ft altitude) — no altitude factor. June weather in Seattle is mild (20-27C), which should suit both sides equally.
Egypt's historical head-to-head dominance (3-1) is primarily composed of friendly results and should not be over-weighted vs a tournament context where Belgium are operationally superior.
Group context: this is Matchday 1 for both teams, so there is no points-pressure asymmetry; both sides are playing to win from the start.
